# Manage customer access

:::note Beta Feature
The Enterprise Portal is Beta. Features described on this page are subject to change. Some capabilities might require additional access.
:::

This topic describes how to give customers access to the new Enterprise Portal, including moving customers from the Classic Enterprise Portal or the Download Portal, and how to manage their portal users from the Vendor Portal.

## Give customers access to the new Enterprise Portal {#give-customers-access}

### Teams using only the new Enterprise Portal

All customers can access the portal. You do not need an app-level or per-customer enable toggle.

### Teams using both portals {#teams-using-both-portals}

If your team also uses the Classic Enterprise Portal or the Download Portal, you can adopt the new Enterprise Portal incrementally. Run the portals side by side, then move customers over individually or all together. All portals share the same backend, so customer data, licenses, and instance information are consistent across them.

#### Portal coexistence

You can run the Download Portal, the Classic Enterprise Portal, and the new Enterprise Portal side by side, with different customers on each, indefinitely. Treat this as an ongoing state, not only a step toward a full migration.

For a single customer, though, these are alternatives, not concurrent options. Turning on Enterprise Portal access for a customer moves that customer off the Download Portal onto whichever portal version their **Portal Version** setting selects.

#### Plan for the address change {#plan-for-the-address-change}

Moving a customer to the new Enterprise Portal changes the address they use to reach it. The Classic Enterprise Portal and Download Portal run at `get.replicated.com/{appSlug}` or your custom domain for those portals. The new Enterprise Portal runs at `{appSlug}.enterpriseportal.app` or a separate custom domain. A single custom domain can't serve both.

Before you move a customer, confirm they can reach the new address. Customers in restricted networks often allowlist the portal address. For them, an unannounced move can make the portal unreachable. Tell customers the new hostname ahead of time, and ask them to allowlist it by hostname, not IP address. For more information about custom domains, see [Configure a custom domain](/vendor/enterprise-portal-v2-domains).

#### Move customers {#move-customers}

Moving a customer to the new Enterprise Portal requires a Vendor Portal team admin. A content repo must be linked before you can move customers.

1. Set up the new Enterprise Portal. In the Vendor Portal, go to **Enterprise Portal** and select **New Portal**. Customers continue using their current portal until you move them.
1. Connect a content repo. Follow the steps in [Connect a Git repo](/vendor/enterprise-portal-v2-connect-repo). Connecting a repo has no effect on any customer's portal version. No customer sees the new portal until you explicitly move them.
1. Test it yourself. Use the local CLI preview (`replicated enterprise-portal preview`) or open the new portal URL directly to see how your content renders. You can also use **Login as customer** on a customer's **Enterprise Portal access** tab. For more information, see [Test and preview the Enterprise Portal](/vendor/enterprise-portal-v2-access).
1. Move individual customers. On the customer's **Enterprise Portal access** tab, set **Portal Version** to **Use new Enterprise Portal for this customer**. This affects only that customer. If the customer doesn't have Enterprise Portal access yet, turn on **Enable Enterprise Portal for this customer** first. The **Portal Version** control only appears after access is on for that customer, either through their own toggle or through the app-level **Enable Enterprise Portal for all customers** override.
1. Move customers back if needed. Set **Portal Version** back to Classic at any time. The customer immediately returns to the Classic experience.
1. Move everyone at the same time, if you don't need a gradual rollout. On **Enterprise Portal > Customer Access**, turn on **Enable Enterprise Portal for all customers** to move every customer, including those on KOTS or kURL, off the Download Portal immediately. This doesn't change any customer's individual access or **Portal Version** setting. It overrides the result while it's on, and turning it back off returns each customer to their individual setting.

To automate these steps with the Vendor API, see [Customer access](/vendor/enterprise-portal-v2-vendor-api-automation#customer-access) in _Headless Enterprise Portal: Vendor API_.

#### Vendor Portal view and customer portal version

When both portals are running for your team, **New Portal** and **Classic Portal** buttons appear at the top of the main Enterprise Portal settings area in the Vendor Portal. These buttons switch which version of the Enterprise Portal settings you see and configure as a vendor. They have no effect on which portal any customer sees. To change a specific customer's portal, use the **Portal Version** setting on that customer's **Enterprise Portal access** tab.

### KOTS and kURL customers {#kots-and-kurl-customers}

The new Enterprise Portal supports KOTS and kURL customers, with some differences from Helm and Embedded Cluster customers. KOTS and kURL application upgrades are performed in the Admin Console, and their instance cards provide target-aware guidance plus application bundle downloads for entitled air gap customers. For details on what these customers see, including current limitations, see [KOTS and kURL instances](/vendor/enterprise-portal-v2-use#kots-and-kurl-instances) in _Log in to and use the Enterprise Portal_.

Moving a KOTS or kURL customer works the same way as moving a Helm or Embedded Cluster customer. The app-level **Enable Enterprise Portal for all customers** option applies to KOTS and kURL customers too.

Most KOTS and kURL customers don't have Enterprise Portal access enabled yet, since they've been using the Download Portal. You need to turn on **Enable Enterprise Portal for this customer** before the **Portal Version** control appears. The Classic Enterprise Portal does not support KOTS or kURL. Leaving **Portal Version** at its default after enabling access does not give the customer a working portal. Set it to **Use new Enterprise Portal for this customer** explicitly.

To automate this instead of using the Vendor Portal UI, use [Patch a customer](https://replicated-vendor-api.readme.io/reference/patchcustomer) with `is_enterprise_portal_enabled: true` to grant access, then [Update Enterprise Portal settings](https://replicated-vendor-api.readme.io/reference/updateenterpriseportalsettings) with `portalVersion: "v2"` to select the new Enterprise Portal.

If you also want this customer to see Security Center, enable access for the customer or for all customers at the app level. Security Center access is separate from **Portal Version**. For a KOTS or kURL customer, Security Center shows an explanatory message instead of security data until they also have a Helm or Embedded Cluster instance. For more information, see [Enable Security Center access](/vendor/security-center-enable-customer-access#enable-security-center-access) in _Enable Customer Access to Security Information_.

## Invite users {#inviting-users}

To invite a customer's end user to the portal:

1. Go to **Customers > [Customer Name] > Enterprise Portal access**
1. In the **Customer Users** section, click **+ Invite user**
1. Enter the user's email address and click **Send invite**
1. The user receives an email with an invitation link to activate their account

You can also enable **Automatically invite customer email to Enterprise Portal on creation** so that every new customer with an email address receives an invite automatically.

For teams using only the new Enterprise Portal, go to **Enterprise Portal > Customer Access**. In the **Customer invitations** section, enable automatic invitations. On teams using both portals, automatic invitations require the app-level **Enable Enterprise Portal for all customers** setting.

On teams using both portals, the customer creation screen includes a **Use new Enterprise Portal for this customer** checkbox. When checked, the customer is enrolled in the new Enterprise Portal and any auto-invite email points them to the new portal URL instead of Classic. This checkbox is only visible to team admins. When unchecked or not visible, new customers default to Classic.

## Access to multiple channels

A license is assigned to a single channel. To give one end user access to releases from more than one channel (for example, a stable channel for production and an alpha channel for a test environment), create a separate customer for each channel, each with a license on the intended channel.

To present these as a single login, invite the same email address to each customer. The user logs in once and switches between the customers using the team switcher in the portal. For the customer-side experience, see [Access with multiple teams](/vendor/enterprise-portal-v2-use#access-with-multiple-teams).

Because each customer appears to the end user as a separate team, name your customers descriptively (for example, `Customer A - Stable` and `Customer A - Alpha`) so users can tell their environments apart.

:::note
Inviting different email addresses to each customer creates separate logins with no team switcher. Use the same email address for each customer to give one person a unified experience.
:::

## Remove users {#removing-users}

To remove a user from a customer's portal team:

1. Go to **Customers > [Customer Name] > Enterprise Portal access**
1. In the **Customer Users** table, click the menu icon (**...**) next to the user
1. Select **Remove user**

## Domain restrictions

Restrict which email domains can be invited to a customer's portal:

1. Go to **Customers > [Customer Name] > Enterprise Portal access**
1. In the **Authentication** section, enable **Domain Restrictions**
1. Add one or more allowed email domains (e.g., `acme.com`)

Only users with email addresses matching an allowed domain can be invited. This prevents accidental invitations to personal email addresses or unauthorized domains. The allowed domain list also governs SAML logins. For more information, see [Just-in-time user provisioning](#jit-provisioning).

## SAML authentication

Allow customers to use their corporate identity provider for portal login. SAML authentication is enabled for all teams by default, so you do not need to request access to it.

1. Go to **Customers > [Customer Name] > Enterprise Portal access**
1. In the **Authentication** section, enable **SAML Authentication**
1. Users on the customer's team can then configure their IdP details (metadata URL, certificates) from the Enterprise Portal's team settings

### Just-in-time user provisioning {#jit-provisioning}

SAML supports just-in-time (JIT) user provisioning, which creates a portal account the first time that a user logs in with SAML. Whether the user also needs a pending invitation depends on where the login starts:

- **IdP-initiated**: the user starts at the identity provider. The portal creates the account with no invitation
- **Portal-initiated**: the user starts at the portal login page. The portal creates the account only if that email address already has a pending invitation, and otherwise returns the `saml_invite_required` error

When **Domain Restrictions** are enabled, the allowed domain list also governs SAML. The portal does not create an account for a user whose email domain is absent from the list, and returns the `domain_not_allowed` error instead. Two details of this check matter in practice:

- It runs before the invitation check, so a new user from a domain that is not allowed sees `domain_not_allowed` even when they also lack an invitation
- It applies only when the portal creates the account. Removing a domain from the list does not lock out users who were already provisioned from it

For the full set of SAML login errors and how to resolve them, see [SAML login errors](/vendor/enterprise-portal-v2-troubleshooting#saml-login-errors) in _Troubleshoot the Enterprise Portal_.

## Service accounts

Service accounts provide programmatic access to the Enterprise Portal (e.g., for CI/CD pipelines pulling install commands or registry credentials).

- View and manage service accounts on the customer's **Enterprise Portal access** tab under **Customer Service Accounts**
- Service accounts are created by users on the customer's team from **Team Settings > Service Accounts** in the Enterprise Portal, automatically when a customer starts a new installation from the portal, and when you create install options through the Vendor API
- A service account can hold more than one token. Users on the customer's team create additional tokens and revoke individual tokens from **Team Settings > Service Accounts**. Use an additional token to give a CI system access to an existing installation without changing the token that the installation runs with. For more information, see [Manage service account tokens](/vendor/enterprise-portal-v2-use#rotate-or-revoke-a-service-account-token) in _Log in to and use the Enterprise Portal_.
- Vendors can revoke service accounts from the Vendor Portal. Revoking a service account stops all of its tokens.
